name: Potential test switch
summary: Panel test switch that opens a VT secondary circuit to a relay or meter so test voltages can be applied safely.
description: A potential test switch is a knife switch in a VT secondary circuit that isolates a relay or meter from the VT so test voltages can be injected. Unlike a current switch it has no shorting contact, because a VT secondary must never be shorted.

When the switch is open, protection that relies on the voltage may be disabled or may see loss of voltage. The symbol does not show that consequence, so the test procedure should list the functions affected and whether any trip outputs must also be isolated.
readingNotes: Confirm there is no shorting contact on VT circuits.
List functions affected when the switch is open.
distinction: A potential test switch opens a voltage circuit; a current test switch shorts the CT before opening.
